1967 Chevrolet Corvette With 3,304 Miles on the Clock Rocks Tuxedo Black Look and 427ci Big Block V8
74 photos
Photo: Motorcar Classics
New York-based Motorcar Classics probably thinks it has you covered if you're willing to write a very fat check for this magnificent ‘Triple Black’ BBC (big block) V8 Chevy Corvette from 1967.
The C8 iteration of ‘America’s sports car’ is quite far and away from the humble beginnings in 1953 when the original fiberglass Corvette was almost killed before it could properly take off because of slow sales. Now, the C8 is an established legend, more than 70 years after it was first conceived.
But it’s also not very accessible anymore. Indeed, after inflation and other hikes, the 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray currently kicks off at no less than $71,300 sans destination for the base Coupe version. It’s a mid-engine sports car now, indeed, and also has a brand-new 6.7-liter V8 engine rocking 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque, which is way more power than a base Corvette used to have back in the days of the C1.
The new engine is shared across the range with the returning Corvette Grand Sport ($86,300) and the all-new, first-ever Corvette Grand Sport X ($110k), which has come to replace the previous E-Ray as the ‘base’ performance hybrid model with all-wheel drive. Its potential? No less than 721 combined horsepower, by the way! Do you want a more expensive Corvette or power of hypercar magnitude? No problem, as the 670-hp homologation Z06 starts from almost $122k, while the Corvette ZR1 and ZR1X (hybrid) have no less than 1,064 hp and 1,250 combined hp, respectively.
Photo: Motorcar Classics Of course, they’re also more expensive: $198k and $227,800 – which is a lot of cash for a Chevrolet, for sure. But since they can go head-to-head and toe-to-toe with the likes of Ferrari, Lamborghini, or McLaren, it’s a small price to pay, right? Well, if you have reached that conclusion – that we only live once and it doesn’t kill you to spend six-figure sums on a Corvette, here’s another proposal: a 1967 Chevrolet Corvette.
Bear with us. This one is for collectors and enthusiasts alike, as it represents the final year of the C2 Corvette, the car that completely rethought the series into the model that was loved for decades until the C8 again rewrote the rule book with a mid-engine configuration. The dealership says this is a “magnificent 1967 Chevrolet Corvette Coupe representing the holy grail of American muscle and the absolute peak of second-generation Sting Ray design.”
It is finished in the desirable and factory-correct Tuxedo Black (Paint Code 900) over Black Leather upholstery (Trim Code 402); it is also contrasted with a striking Red Stinger hood, and the rare "Triple Black" big-block coupe also has the fancy chrome side exhaust “loudspeakers” along with the amplifier to make them rumble – a matching-numbers 427 cubic-inch L71 big-block V8 engine, factory-rated at ‘just’ 435 horsepower and 460 lb-ft of torque.
Photo: Motorcar Classics The engine is packing the iconic “Tri-Power” setup featuring three two-barrel Holley carburetors atop an aluminum intake manifold and is also paired with a four-speed manual transmission, so “this Corvette delivers visceral performance amplified by factory side-exit exhaust pipes with original-style heat shields and transistor ignition.” The car has gone through a “labor-intensive frame-off restoration reportedly requiring more than 2,200 man-hours and over $70,000 in parts and materials.” Cool, right?
Additionally, the chassis features power-assisted four-wheel disc brakes, power steering, and an independent rear suspension with a transverse leaf spring, plus a Positraction 3.70 ratio AO rear axle, and the car sits on beautiful, classic 15-inch turbine-style wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich Silvertown radial tires with fancy red lines, “striking the perfect balance between original aesthetics and modern drivability.”
It’s going to be a show offering, as the company explains that “every detail was meticulously addressed to meet stringent judging standards, down to correct head markings on the hardware throughout the vehicle and an undercarriage that remains as immaculate as the exterior.” It has already received multiple NCRS Top Flight awards, so the C2 with its original L71 427/435 HP engine is not only dressed to impress but also ready to roll on the show floor.
Photo: Motorcar Classics There are also a bevy of options on board, like the power steering, power brakes, power windows, tinted glass, and a vertical push-button AM/FM radio. The sale comes with “a rich documentation package, including a photocopy of the original factory tank sticker, the original Protect-O-Plate, manufacturer's literature, a reproduction window sticker, dynamic dyno test results, and official NCRS judging sheets,” among other things.
Of course, this “turnkey crown jewel ready for high-level concours display or private collection preservation” is not selling cheap: the dealership has a stated price of $289,900, but you can still negotiate through the ‘make an offer’ button on their online sales portal. So, what do you think – yay or nay? Would you buy somethign like this or a brand-new ZR1X with this kind of money?
